newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt land auction seen next week's market focus.
newsitem.headline: HK govt land auction seen next week's market focus.

text.p: The Hong Kong government is set to hold this year's first land auction next week and mounting expectations that curbs will soon be imposed on property speculators will make the event a market focus, analysts said.
Two plots of land located in Repulse Bay, on the south side of Hong Kong island, and Tuen Mun in the New Territories, will be auctioned in public on Wednesday.
"The results will be considered as a barometer for developers' confidence to the market on possible government intervention," one property analyst said.
The Tuen Mun site is for mass residential use and the Repulse Bay site for luxury housing.
Residential property prices rose an average of 24 percent last year and the government has said there were signs of speculation in the luxury end of the market.

With the luxury end of the market under close scrutiny, China Everbright research director Patrick Chia said the Repulse Bay site would make the auction a focus. "Because there are some uncertainties in the property market that will affect the developers' confidence in the property market," he said.
Cheng Wing Ming, a director of Chung Sen Surveyors Ltd, said there was talk the government could act soon.
"People are speculating that the government could announce some measures to curb speculation on properties during the middle of next week," he said.
But he said concerns were unlikely to cool developers' enthusiasm and the auction should attract active bidding from large to medium-sized developers.
Property consultants said the Repulse Bay plot of 2,008 square metres (21,614 sq ft), with expected gross floor area of about 700 square metres (12,529 sq ft), was earmarked for low rise buildings.
They expected the land to be sold at between HK$179 million to 188 million or HK$14,000 to HK$15,000 per square foot.
The Tuen Mun site of 5,080 square metres (54,681 square foot), with gross floor area estimated at 3,965 square metres (71,085), was for mass housing.
It was expected to fetch between HK$178 million and HK$200 million or HK$2,500 to HK$2,800 per square foot. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
